chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A woman came seeking redress against a Bedouin who had frightened her, so she miscarried her fetus.
The Bedouin said: “It did not cry out, nor did it make a sound, and the like of this is disregarded without compensation.”
So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said to him: “Be quiet, O rhyming speaker. Upon you is a ghurrah: a male slave or a female slave.”

key_terms.أَفْزَعَهَا: frightened her; caused fear leading to harm
key_terms.عَبْدٌ أَوْ أَمَةٌ: a male slave or female slave as the assessed compensation
key_terms.غُرَّةٌ: the prescribed compensation for a miscarried fetus
key_terms.يُطَلُّ: to be left uncompensated or disregarded in blood-money claims

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for causing a woman to miscarry her fetus in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a case in which a woman miscarried after being frightened by a Bedouin, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله imposed liability upon him. It indicates a legal ruling for compensation in the case of a miscarried fetus and rejects the argument that the absence of crying or audible life removes responsibility.
